<thought>The 1H NMR spectra indicate the presence of aromatic protons (around 7.15 and 7.92 ppm), a methoxy group (singlet at 3.81 ppm), and aliphatic protons (multiplets around 1.20, 2.85, and 3.09 ppm). The combination of these shifts suggests a structure with an aromatic ring, a methoxy group, and possibly an ester or ketone group. To further refine the structure, I will check the IR spectra for functional group confirmation, especially for carbonyl groups.</thought>
<action>ir_spectra</action>
<action_input>{}</action_input>

<thought>The IR spectra show a strong peak at 1739 cm⁻¹, which is indicative of a carbonyl group, likely an ester or ketone. The presence of peaks around 3100-3000 cm⁻¹ suggests aromatic C-H stretching, consistent with the aromatic protons observed in the 1H NMR. The combination of these data suggests a methoxy-substituted aromatic ester. To narrow down the possible structures, I will use the mass spectrometry data to determine the molecular weight and further confirm the molecular formula.</thought>
<action>mass_spectrometry_spectra</action>
<action_input>{}</action_input>

<thought>The mass spectrometry data shows a major peak at m/z 193, which likely corresponds to the molecular ion peak, suggesting a molecular weight of 193 g/mol. Given the presence of a methoxy group, aromatic ring, and carbonyl group, a plausible structure could be methyl benzoate (C8H8O2). To confirm this, I will generate the chemical formula from the SMILES string of methyl benzoate and compare it with the expected molecular weight.</thought>
<action>get_formula_from_smiles</action>
<action_input>{"smiles": "COC(=O)C1=CC=CC=C1"}</action_input>
